summary: Streaming final paragraph lost during connection handoff when heartbeat suppressed on client sleep
description: Customer reports that when a mobile user (Android, Chrome) transitions between Wi-Fi networks or the device enters a deep-sleep power-save state, the streamed response frequently arrives without the final paragraph and closing metadata. The visible stream contains all earlier paragraphs plus a keepalive/heartbeat chunk, then the connection is re-established but the final paragraph is missing. This differs from typical partial-token cases: the finalization marker ("event: end") is not observed in logs for affected sessions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use ClarionDocs integration to call chat-completion streaming endpoint with a 2-3 paragraph prompt that returns a multi-paragraph finalization.

2) On Android (Chrome), start on office Wi-Fi, then trigger a switch to cellular or force the device into background (simulated via Developer Options -> Dont keep activities / or use Nexus 6 emulator with network toggles).
3) Observe SSE/ws stream in client SDK (v1.8.3) — note heartbeat chunks and then an immediate re-open. Final paragraph is not present; client sees stream end without closing metadata.
4) Replaying the same request from a desktop client or keeping the connection stable does not reproduce the missing-final-paragraph behavior.
5) Attach full HAR and SDK debug output captured from the mobile client session.
6) Confirm server-side logs for the request id (included in logs_snippets) show no "finalize" event delivered to the connection that was torn down.
expected_behavior: When the client experiences transient network handoff or sleep, the server should either deliver the finalization marker before connection teardown or allow the resumed session to request the missing tail (idempotent resume) so the final paragraph is re-emitted.
actual_behavior: Affected sessions show a keepalive/heartbeat chunk then an abrupt disconnect; after reconnect, client receives full stream up to but excluding final paragraph and the closing metadata event. There is no explicit server-side error; connection logs show a graceful close from upstream LB in some cases.
logs_snippets: 2026-03-10T15:12:08.723Z INFO request=cli-83f72 stream_chunk=\"data: {\"choices\": [{\"delta\": \"...final paragraph part 1\"}]}\" conn_id=az-01-7ff
2026-03-10T15:12:11.615Z DEBUG sdk-client: last_event=\"data\":\"...\" client-log: \"stream closed without end event\"
comments: 2026-03-10 16:05 - Aisha Patel (Support) : Customer provided HAR and mobile SDK logs. Reproduced once with device simulator. Raising to infra for possible LB keepalive behavior.

2026-03-10 18:15 - Mateo Ruiz (SRE) : Noticed \"upstream_close=keepalive_timeout\" in logs. Possible scenario: LB gracefully closes idle connections on perceived inactivity while mobile in deep-sleep; keepalive is coalesced behind NAT causing suppressed heartbeats.

2026-03-11 09:02 - Ethan Monroe (Engineer) : Added debug flags to serving runtime for seq-tracking. Observed that finalizer logic is gated on ack of last-token write; if TCP/HTTP pipeline is closed mid-flush by LB without EOR propagation, finalizer is not emitted to fallback resume token store.
2026-03-11 11:40 - Aisha Patel (Support) : Customer confirms behavior happens ~8% of mobile streams during commutes. They asked for immediate workaround; they cannot change network conditions.
investigation_notes: - Reproduced on Android emulator when toggling cellular/Wi-Fi; not reproduced on desktop.
- Grafana trace for request cli-83f72: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/stream-traces?orgId=1&var-request=cli-83f72 shows LB idle_teardown at 2.3s after last payload write.
- Correlated with frontend LB config: idle timeout 2s for h2->h1 translation path. This explains upstream_close=keepalive_timeout entries.

- Serving runtime currently relies on in-memory 'end-event' emission during final token write; if upstream connection closes before the write is ACKed, we do not persist the end-event to the resume store.

- Hypothesis: Connection handoff combined with coalesced keepalives leads to server not observing final write completion; LB issues a graceful close which our pipeline treats as normal close and skips persisting finalize state.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11): Increase LB idle timeout for streaming h2->h1 path from 2s to 10s for customer-dedicated pool. This reduced occurrences in ClarionDocs traffic from ~8% to ~1.2% in a 24h window.

Code fix (in review): Persist finalize marker to resume-store before acknowledging final token write to connection; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2245 (adds durable end-event write).
Customer workaround: Enable client-side resume logic in SDK v1.8.3 by providing last_received_seq as resume param. ClarionDocs adopted this in their mobile SDK to request missing tail on reconnect.
Status: Partial fix deployed to customer pool + runtime PR in review. Closing pending confirmation of patch and infra rollback plan for LB timeouts if needed.
follow_up_actions: 1) Merge PR #2245 and release runtime v1.12.0 that durably persists end-event (owner: Ethan Monroe, ETA 2026-03-17).
2) Create infra ticket INT-82012 to audit LB idle timeout across streaming paths and set sane defaults for mobile-heavy pools (owner: Mateo Ruiz).
3) Update Streaming Handoff Runbook to include step: if keepalive coalescing observed, temporarily raise LB idle timeout and enable resume-store debugging (owner: On-call SRE).
4) Recommend SDK change: make resume-by-seq automatic for v1.9+ and document in breaking-changes (owner: Developer Experience).
